nominees.name: Phil Weiser
team: Jena Griswold, Colorado Secretary of State, is the Democratic nominee for Attorney General (Foley Hoag); not an appointee.

positions.stance: Increase attainable owner-occupied homes by 40,000; stands with renters; commentary notes few specifics.

'Primary care for all'; strengthen the Colorado Option; doubts a full public option, would study single-payer; challenge hospital consolidation, surprise billing and medical debt; safety-net stabilization task force for federal cuts; continue insulin caps and drug-price enforcement.
Protect elections, reproductive and LGBTQ+ rights, public lands and fair representation; early supporter of emergency redistricting, which Polis opposed.
Would not support the Worker Protection Act that Polis vetoed twice.
His office has sued the Trump administration almost 70 times.

policyShifts.shift: Systemwide shift toward primary care and consolidation scrutiny.
Continued litigation posture; commentary asks about 'uncooperative federalism' but he has not committed.
Support for a mid-decade map change (a ballot measure question raised in commentary).

impediments.title: Federal funding cuts
impediments.detail: Safety-net stabilization task force proposed in response to federal cuts.

impediments.title: Budget and TABOR
impediments.detail: The commentary did not cover revenue plans or TABOR constraints; a known structural constraint to verify.

impediments.title: Differences from Polis
impediments.detail: Redistricting split; style shift; some continuity on immigration data-sharing positions.

insights: Continuity-with-reset: same party as Polis, so agency heads can be retained, but Weiser's health and litigation agenda favors appointees from his AG office (inference).
AG succession (Griswold is the Democratic nominee) means the new governor and AG would be close allies; the AG's race status was not checked here.

analysis.timing: Inauguration expected Jan. 12, 2027 (second Tuesday in January; verify).
